concerns.text: Consumer before Producer violation: Task T022 (Extract time series) depends on motion-filtered data, but Task T015 (Create motion exclusion filter) is listed as a separate task in Phase 3 without a clear dependency marker or ordering guarantee. T022 cannot execute if T015 is not completed first, yet the phase structure implies parallel execution of US1 tasks.

Atlas dependency violation: Task T021 (Implement AAL atlas DMN region extraction) is marked [P] (parallel-safe) and placed in Phase 4, but it is a prerequisite for T022 (Time series extraction) and T023 (Correlation matrix). The current ordering allows T022/T023 to be scheduled before T021, breaking the data-flow dependency.

Meta-analysis dependency violation: Task T034 (Implement random-effects meta-analysis) requires effect sizes from US2 (T027/T032). The current structure places T034 in Phase 5 but does not explicitly enforce that US2 tasks must complete before US3 tasks begin, risking a scenario where meta-analysis runs on missing or uncomputed effect sizes.

Power analysis ordering violation: Task T019 (Implement post-hoc power analysis) is placed in Phase 2 (Foundational), but post-hoc power analysis requires observed effect sizes from US2 (T027). This task is semantically impossible to execute before US2 is complete, violating the 'producer before consumer' rule.

Ambiguous parallel tag: Task T016 (Nilearn fallback) is marked [P] but is described as an 'independent alternative' to T013. If T016 is truly independent, it should not be in the same phase as T013 without a clear 'OR' logic or dependency on T013 failure. The [P] tag may be misleading if the tasks are mutually exclusive alternatives rather than parallel concurrent tasks.
